Posted by Joyce Ramirez on Mar 21st, 2018 // No Comments 
Hanseatic Management Services Inc. cut its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 50.5% in the 3rd quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The fund owned 29,220 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 29,813 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up 5.1% of Hanseatic Management Services Inc.’s portfolio, making the stock its largest holding. Hanseatic Management Services Inc.’s holdings in Apple were worth $4,503,000 as of its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 
Several other large investors also recently bought and sold shares of the company. Schnieders Capital Management LLC lifted its position in Apple by 3.6% in the second quarter. Schnieders Capital Management LLC now owns 41,583 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,989,000 after purchasing an additional 1,435 shares during the period. DT Investment Partners LLC lifted its position in Apple by 46.3% in the second quarter. DT Investment Partners LLC now owns 2,684 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $387,000 after purchasing an additional 850 shares during the period. Alpha Cubed Investments LLC lifted its position in Apple by 15.6% in the second quarter. Alpha Cubed Investments LLC now owns 231,712 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $33,371,000 after purchasing an additional 31,227 shares during the period. Eagle Global Advisors LLC lifted its position in Apple by 1.6% in the second quarter. Eagle Global Advisors LLC now owns 210,143 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $30,265,000 after purchasing an additional 3,340 shares during the period. Finally, Probity Advisors Inc. lifted its position in Apple by 1.7% in the second quarter. Probity Advisors Inc. now owns 4,789 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $690,000 after purchasing an additional 80 shares during the period. 61.33% of the stock is owned by institutional investors. A number of brokerages have recently commented on AAPL. Vetr downgraded Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $178.34 price objective for the company. in a research report on Friday, December 1st. UBS set a $190.00 price objective on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Friday, January 5th. Morgan Stanley reiterated a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 price objective (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Tuesday, January 23rd. Sanford C. Bernstein lowered Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and reduced their target price for the company from $195.00 to $170.00 in a report on Friday, February 2nd. Finally, HSBC set a $204.00 target price on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Tuesday, January 30th. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, eighteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have given a buy rating and one has issued a strong buy rating to the company. Apple presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $201.53. 
In other Apple news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of Apple stock in a transaction on Friday, January 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total transaction of $2,733,733.98. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 13,739 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $2,401,302.42. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available through this hyperlink . 0.06% of the stock is currently owned by insiders. 
Apple ( AAPL ) traded down $0.06 on Tuesday, reaching $175.24. 19,602,195 shares of the company’s stock were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 37,462,656. The company has a quick ratio of 1.20, a current ratio of 1.24 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. Apple has a 12-month low of $138.62 and a 12-month high of $183.50. The firm has a market cap of $903,275.88, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.01, a PEG ratio of 1.34 and a beta of 1.19. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 EPS for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the business earned $3.36 EPS. The business’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. equities analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.43 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
